Senses.Explanation: To receive someone and lead them onward. In Chan records it commonly names reception of students by named teachers and the answers given when students come before them. Asked, “how do you receive and lead?” (作麼生接引), Juelang Daosheng answers, “every house has a road open to carts and horses” (家家有路通車馬). Konggu Daocheng, asked “by which gate do you receive and lead later students?” (以那一門接引後學), answers with the recorded alternatives of staff and shout, expedient and actual, opposing and following. An unnamed questioner says, “I too hope to be received and led” (某甲亦望接引), and Konggu replies, “one cannot walk by taking another by the hand; only one's own assent is intimate” (把手牽人行不得，為人自肯乃方親). Qianshan Hanke asks whether the fundamental matter can be used to receive people, then sets “if there is receiving” against “without relying on receiving” (若有接引；不假接引). Thus the corpus uses an ordinary verb of reception as a category for named teachers' dealings with arrivals, while also recording challenges to the category itself; it supplies no single fixed procedure under the word.

Senses.Explanation: To cast aside cause and effect is a named and condemned error: treating conduct and consequence as though they can simply be denied. The Record of Gu Xue Zhe says that misconstruing the ancients’ situation-matched talk can lead people to cast aside cause and effect and invite calamity. The Record of Gu Ting places the error after laziness gives rise to wild thoughts, and the Complete Record of Juelang asks how cause and effect could be cast aside when speaking of individual and shared karma. Dahui’s formal discourse likewise warns that hearing emptiness and then denying cause and effect is an error. The two stored expression-by-negation controls define expression by negation but do not themselves contain the no-cause-and-no-effect formula; they therefore mark a comparison that must be made from exact speech frames, not a license to equate every negative formula with causal denial.

The tiny mustard seed is the records’ scale-comparison object, repeatedly paired with reversals in which Mount Sumeru is contained within it. The graphs name a mustard seed. The allowlisted corpus has 442 hits in 146 texts. Its small size supplies the comparison ‘mustard-seed-sized’ (芥子許, 67 hits in 50 texts), as when a named record subject speaks of a doubt as small as a mustard seed. The corpus also repeatedly pairs the seed with Mount Sumeru in both directions: ‘Sumeru contains a mustard seed’ (須彌納芥子, 46 hits in 30 texts) and ‘a mustard seed contains Sumeru’ (芥子納須彌, 59 hits in 44 texts). In the Guizong encounter, Li Bo accepts the first statement but asks whether the second is false; Guizong asks where Li Bo’s ten thousand books are held in a body the size of a coconut. In another exchange, the two directions receive the one-word answers ‘easy’ and ‘difficult.’ A later address records mountains, earth, trees, monastics, laypeople, sages, and ordinary people placed inside a mustard seed without the seed becoming narrow. These are the corpus’s recorded scale constructions; the entry does not turn them into a symbolic meaning for the seed.
Senses.Note: All required definition formulas were searched. One ‘What is the mustard seed?’ question is included because its answer, ‘It blocks your eye,’ is an attested direct response, not adopted here as a universal lexical equation. Deployment inventory includes the small-measure construction, both Sumeru constructions, question-and-answer use, and a later expanded list of what is placed inside the seed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 須彌芥子父。芥子須彌爺。山水坦然平。敲氷來煮茶。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (圓悟佛果禪師語錄). Fu Dashi is the exact actor: the quoted Fu Dashi verse says (須彌芥子父)，(芥子須彌爺).

Senses.Explanation: ‘Mount Sumeru enters a mustard seed’ places an enormous mountain inside a tiny seed. Jiangzhou prefect Li Bo explicitly utters the question in three recensions of his exchange with Guizong Zhichang; those witnesses are one case, not three independent deployments. A separate monastic question in the Patriarchs’ Hall Collection asks the same formula in an independently recorded exchange whose respondent is not identified by this stored cut.
